title: Reliability Onramp: zero-to-one program plan
content:
Purpose and framing:
This doc is a pragmatic cross-functional program plan to take feature teams from zero SLO coverage to a minimally viable SLO-program integration ("zero-to-one") suitable for production rollouts. The goal is a repeatable, low-friction path that product, platform, and SRE teams can run in 6–10 weeks per pilot team.

Why this exists (quick):
- Many teams want reliability guarantees but lack standard templates and a validated onboarding ritual.
- We need a lean, observable-first play to accelerate SLO adoption while avoiding heavy process overhead.
- This program codifies a short checklist, workshops, and automation to reduce manual work and handoffs.

Success criteria (end of pilot):
- Each pilot service has at least one key availability and one latency SLO defined and instrumented.
- Error budget alerting wired to pager/ops rotation and a committed mitigation runbook exists.
- Runbook + incident playbook tested via tabletop and one simulated degradation exercise.
- Dashboard with tokenized cost/latency per route (observable) and telemetry collection rate >= 95%.

Scope (what we will do in a pilot):
- Discovery workshop (1 week): identify owner, critical paths, user journeys, and target SLIs.
- Instrumentation sprint (2 weeks): add SLIs (success rate, p95/p99 latency), export to observability backend.
- SLO definition workshop (1 week): set targets, burn rate policies, and alert thresholds.
- Runbook + integration (1 week): create runbooks, configure alerting, hook into incident channels.
- Cutover & validation (1 week): canary SLO enforcement, tabletop test, retro + handoff.

Program timeline (high level, pilot example):
- Week 0: Kickoff + discovery
- Weeks 1–2: Instrumentation & observability work
- Week 3: SLO target setting + alert policy decisions
- Week 4: Runbook and pager integration
- Week 5: Canary validation and exercise
- Week 6: Handoff, docs, and retrospective
Note: For teams with heavy instrumentation debt add two extra weeks.

Stakeholders and roles (recommended):
- Product owner (team): prioritizes SLI scope and accepts SLO targets.
- Service owner / Tech lead (team): implements instrumentation and deploys changes.
- SRE Onramp Lead (SRE): runs workshops, validates SLIs, sets burn rate rules, and owns canary policy.
- Observability engineer: assists with dashboards, sampling, and alerts.
- Platform/Infra contact: resolves platform-level telemetry and quotas (batching, retention).
- Security/Compliance rep (if required): approves any data-path changes and audit logging.
- Customer Success (as needed): maps SLOs to customer-facing commitments.

Rituals and collaboration pattern (what to run each week):
- Weekly 60-minute working sync (product + tech lead + SRE + obs).
- Twice-weekly office hours drop-in (SRE + obs) for implementation blockers.
- Slack channel: #onramp-{service}-reliability (pin workshop notes, runbooks, and sprint PRs).
- Confluence page template: one page per pilot with a checklist and progress status.

Deliverables per pilot (templates included):
- Discovery notes (one-pager)
- SLI instrument list (metric name, source, calc)
- SLO definition document (target, periodicity, window, burn policy)
- Runbook + escalation path (with play links)
- Observability dashboard (baseline p95/p99, throughput, errors)
- Post-mortem + retro notes (lessons and action items)

Example SLO template (minimal):
- SLO name: "api-main success rate"
- SLI: ratio of 2xx to total requests over 30d rolling window
- Target: 99.5% (30d)
- Alert: burn-rate > 4x sustained for 1h OR error rate delta > 0.5% from baseline
- Runbook link: Confluence/reference-runbooks/api-success-rate

Instrumentation checklist (quick):
- [ ] Instrument success/failure counter and latency histogram
- [ ] Correlate traces to customer request id when available
- [ ] Emit telemetry with stable tag schema: service, route, region, env
- [ ] Ensure sampling preserves error traces
- [ ] Validate metrics ingestion and retention in obs backend

Onramp sprint plan (two-week sprint example):
- Sprint kickoff + backlog grooming (day 0)
- Day 1–3: Add counters, histograms, and trace annotations
- Day 4–6: Export metrics -> observability, create queries & dashboards
- Day 7: SLO workshop with product to select targets
- Day 8–10: Implement alerting rules and runbook stub
- Day 11–14: Canary, tabletop exercise, and finalize docs

Gating and rollout policy (minimal viable gate):
- Gate 1: Metrics validated in staging + SLI matches expected distribution
- Gate 2: SLO defined and burn-rate alert configured with a playbook
- Gate 3: On-call aware and escalation path verified (pager test)
- If any gate fails, automatic fallback to a higher-latency tolerant route or scaled capacity until remediated.

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Instrumentation incomplete or high-cardinality metrics overload obs.
  Mitigation: Sampling guidance, cardinality cap, obs engineer support.
- Risk: SLO targets set too tight causing noise and alert fatigue.
  Mitigation: Start conservative, run 30d baseline, adopt progressive tightening (30/60/90-day).
- Risk: Cross-team coordination delays (product/infra dependencies).
  Mitigation: Early discovery, explicit dependency list, and weekly SLA for blockers.

Measurement and KPIs for program health (tracking across pilots):
- Number of pilot services completing zero-to-one per quarter (target: 4/Q).
- Median time from kickoff to SLO live (target: <= 6 weeks).
- Percentage of SLOs with runbooks and tested pager flow (target: 90%).
- Reduction in repeat incidents for pilot services after 3 months (target: -25%).

Operating playbook snippets (copy into per-service runbook):
- Pager triggers: what to do in first 5m, 15m, 1h.
- Immediate mitigation steps: traffic divert, scale up, circuit-breaker toggle.
- Post-incident steps: collect logs/traces, create incident ticket, link SLO burn.

Handoff checklist (to service team from SRE):
- [ ] Confluence runbook signed off by service owner
- [ ] Alerting thresholds and notifications validated
- [ ] On-call escalation tested and contact updated
- [ ] Dashboard baseline screenshots captured and stored
- [ ] Post-mortem template created for future incidents

Communication plan (internal + external):
- Internal: Weekly status note in #reliability-program; biweekly summary to Eng leadership.
- External (customers): For any SLO changes that affect customer promises, pre-announce to affected accounts via CSM.

Dependencies and blockers to watch for:
- Observability quota/retention limits (raise tickets early: JIRA: OBS-2987).
- Feature flags/platform primitives required for canary (Infra epic: REL-3412).
- Security review if metrics contain PII (chat with security, timeline 2–3 business days).

Scaling the program (after 2 pilots):
- Turn templates into a self-serve "onramp kit" (Confluence + terraform/monitoring modules).
- Run an SLO office-hours rotation staffed by SREs and Observability engineers.
- Build automated checks that validate instrumentation coverage at PR time.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Decision: Minimum SLO window we standardize on (30d vs 90d) — propose 30d for rapid feedback, 90d for long-term reviews.
- Decision: Burn-rate alert cadence and throttling policy for auto-remediation — need input from platform.
- Question: Capacity to support more than 4 pilots concurrently without extra headcount? (estimate: need +1 SRE per 4 pilots).

Next steps (for today):
- Book discovery workshop with Team X and Product (owner: Aisha) — target: 2026-03-18.
- Create per-team Confluence page from template and invite obs + SRE.
- Raise OBS-2987 retention increase request if pilot ingestion projected >20GB/day.

Notes to self (working doc style):
- Keep workshop material <30 slides, heavy on examples and live queries.
- Demo: use sample service with a flaky backend to show burn-rate behavior and canary rollback.
- Collect a short library of runbook play snippets we can paste into each pilot.

Appendix: useful links and snippets
- Confluence onramp template: https://redwood-confluence/internal/reliability/onramp-zero-to-one
- Example Jira epics: REL-3412 (platform canary primitives), OBS-2987 (obs retention), REL-3499 (runbook automation)
